questions.title: JavaScript Microtasks Execution Priority
questions.question: Given the following code, in what order are messages logged to the console?
questions.explanation: Synchronous code runs first (`1`, then `4`). Then the microtask queue (`Promise.then`) is completely drained before macrotasks, logging `3`. Finally, the macrotask (`setTimeout`) executes, logging `2`.
hints: Remember that Promises enter the Microtask Queue, while setTimeout enters the Macrotask Queue.

questions.title: React useCallback Dependency Equality
questions.question: Why does the following child component still re-render when the parent updates unrelated state?
options: React.memo does not work with buttons
The `style={{ margin: 10 }}` inline object creates a new reference on every parent render
useCallback needs doSomething in its dependency array
Child components inside useCallback always re-render
questions.explanation: `React.memo` does a shallow comparison (`Object.is`) of props. Even though `onClick` maintains referential equality via `useCallback`, the `style={{ margin: 10 }}` object is allocated anew on every parent render, failing shallow equality.
hints: Look closely at the `style` prop passed to Child.

questions.title: CSS Layout Box Sizing
questions.question: What is the total rendered width of an element with `width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid black; box-sizing: border-box;`?
questions.explanation: With `box-sizing: border-box`, the specified `width` encompasses content, padding, and borders. Therefore the total rendered width is strictly 200px.
hints: border-box subtracts padding and border from the content area.

questions.title: Core Web Vitals - INP Optimization
questions.question: Which browser API is specifically recommended to yield execution back to the main thread during long-running tasks to improve Interaction to Next Paint (INP)?
questions.explanation: `scheduler.yield()` is the modern web standard specifically designed to break long tasks into discrete chunks and yield to the browser's rendering queue, lowering INP delay.
hints: It's part of the new Prioritized Task Scheduling API.

questions.title: TypeScript Discriminated Unions
questions.question: What makes a union type 'discriminated' in TypeScript?
options: It uses the `any` keyword to bypass checking
Every member in the union shares a common literal property key with distinct values
It requires classes instead of interfaces
It is defined inside a namespace
questions.explanation: A discriminated union features a shared singleton literal property (e.g. `type: 'success' | 'error'`) that TypeScript uses to narrow down the exact variant inside conditional blocks.
hints: Think about the common 'tag' or 'kind' property.

questions.title: Next.js Server Component Boundaries
questions.question: Can an async React Server Component (RSC) import and render a Client Component with the 'use client' directive?
options: No, Client Components cannot be rendered inside Server Components
Yes, Server Components can import and render Client Components and pass serializable props
Only if wrapped in an iframe
questions.explanation: Server Components seamlessly import and render Client Components as leaf nodes or interactive subtrees, passing serializable data as props across the network boundary.
hints: Server components act as the outer shell.

questions.title: HTTP Cache-Control Directives
questions.question: Which Cache-Control directive instructs browsers to validate cached content with the origin server before using it?
questions.explanation: `no-cache` does NOT mean 'do not cache'. It means the browser CAN store the response in cache, but MUST revalidate with the origin server (using ETag or If-Modified-Since) before serving it.

questions.title: Web Accessibility (A11y)
questions.question: What is the primary role of the `aria-live='polite'` attribute?
options: It instructs screen readers to announce dynamic content updates when the user is idle
It hides the element from screen readers completely
questions.explanation: `aria-live='polite'` notifies assistive technology to queue and announce DOM mutations when the screen reader finishes speaking the current utterance, avoiding rude interruptions.

questions.title: State Architecture: TanStack Query
questions.question: In TanStack Query, what does `staleTime: 5000` mean?
options: The query will be deleted from cache after 5 seconds
Data is considered fresh for 5 seconds; background refetches won't trigger on window focus during this window
The browser caches the HTTP response for 5000 seconds
questions.explanation: `staleTime` dictates how long data remains fresh. While fresh, queries read directly from cache without initiating network revalidations on component mounts or window focuses.
hints: Compare staleTime with gcTime (garbage collection time).

questions.title: Preventing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)
questions.question: What is the most effective CSS technique to prevent CLS when loading dynamic remote images?
options: Specifying explicit `width` and `height` attributes or CSS `aspect-ratio` on image containers
questions.explanation: By declaring `aspect-ratio` or explicit dimensions, the browser calculates layout space before the image binary downloads, preventing layout shifts.
hints: The browser needs to reserve space upfront.
